If the Claude Code template and its generated docs view both contain the new prose but remain stamped `ddflow=0.2.0 sha=5942a35e0678` while the other driver deltas are `ddflow=0.2.9`, every assertion in this test passes: the prose substrings are present, `view == text` holds because the docs view was regenerated from the same stale template, and no assertion compares the stamp to the current version or to the other driver deltas. chunk_findings.detail: The new wave-loop contract says each wave is one `ddflow next --json` read and that the ready set is fanned out to one task subagent per claimed item, and it calls `/mcp__ddflow__implement` “the same command without `/loop`.” But the same paragraph then says a one-shot invocation “falls back to ONE task.” Given a one-shot MCP call when `ddflow next --json` returns two independent ready tasks (for example one `tier:fast` and one `tier:balanced`), this instruction tells the driver to dispatch only one task and stop with a handoff, leaving the other ready task unclaimed. That contradicts the stated fan-out wave contract and makes the MCP path materially different from the looped path, not merely lacking continuation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md:1 (`/mcp__ddflow__implement`)

data.probe: The ONE-task fallback IS the wave contract for a one-shot runtime — the operator's own brief says 'on a one-shot harness, fall back to ONE task and print ddflow next as handoff', and the accepted kilo-cline.md carries the identical clause ('fall back to ONE task, then print ddflow next and ddflow cadence as the handoff', f91600e39). A one-shot invocation CANNOT loop, so it claims one item; the printed handoff is the wave continuation and the next invocation starts by reading next again — the remaining ready item is never abandoned, only deferred to the next read. The finding penalizes the looped path's ceiling, not a regression this diff introduced.
data.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md:1 (`/mcp__ddflow__implement`)
